sections.title: Cheating
sections.summary: Deceiving a person to induce delivery of property or valuable security, causing wrongful loss.

sections.title: Cheating by personation
sections.summary: Cheating by pretending to be another person, or by knowingly substituting one person for another.

sections.title: Extortion
sections.summary: Putting a person in fear of injury to induce delivery of property or valuable security.

sections.title: Criminal breach of trust
sections.summary: Dishonest misappropriation of property entrusted to a person.

sections.title: Criminal intimidation
sections.summary: Threatening a person with injury to person, reputation, or property to cause alarm.

sections.title: Stalking
sections.summary: Monitoring or repeatedly contacting a person despite disinterest, including online monitoring/contact.

sections.title: Voyeurism
sections.summary: Capturing or publishing images of a person engaging in a private act without consent.

sections.title: Kidnapping
sections.summary: Taking or enticing a minor or person of unsound mind out of lawful guardianship, or abduction.

sections.title: Common intention
sections.summary: Acts done by several persons in furtherance of a common intention make each person liable as if done alone.

sections.title: Summons to produce document or thing
sections.summary: Empowers a court/police officer to require production of a document or thing necessary for investigation.

sections.title: Search and seizure procedure
sections.summary: Procedure governing search of place and seizure of property/documents during investigation.

sections.title: Procedure for investigation
sections.summary: General procedure to be followed by police in conducting an investigation.

sections.title: Admissibility of electronic records
sections.summary: Conditions under which electronic records are admissible as evidence, including the certificate requirement.

sections.title: Proof of contents of electronic records via certificate
sections.summary: Requires an accompanying certificate identifying the electronic record and describing the manner of production for it to be admitted.
